content.overview: Plant and material identity must remain reconstructable through propagation, room movement, harvest, sampling, transfer, storage and waste workflows.

vocabulary.definition: Controlled information that distinguishes one plant, batch, lot, container, room, sample or material from another.
The documented relationship linking source material to derived plants, batches or lots.
The ability to reconstruct identity, movement, transformation and disposition from reliable records.

sections.title: Identity is operational infrastructure
sections.body: Reliable identity connects cultivation observations, treatment history, room placement, harvest, samples and downstream records to the correct material. Losing identity can make otherwise accurate data unusable and may force a hold or disposition decision.

sections.title: Verify every transition
sections.body: Risk rises during cloning, transplanting, room moves, container changes, harvest, sampling and handoff. Before a movement, the technician verifies the physical identifier against the work order and destination; after movement, the controlled record should match physical reality.

workedExamples: A tag does not match the room-move order, so movement stops before identity can be lost.
A new harvest container identifier is linked to its source material instead of replacing the earlier identity without history.
commonMistakes: Treating all plants in one room as interchangeable identities.
Removing an old identifier before the replacement is verified and linked.
content.practicalApplication: Trace a mock propagation-to-harvest genealogy through several handoffs and identify where identity could be lost or become ambiguous.
content.summary: Traceability begins with disciplined identity control. Technicians verify identifiers before movement and preserve genealogy through every handoff.

blocks.title: Identity connects every later fact to the correct material
blocks.body: Measurements, observations, treatments, movements, harvest records, samples, storage records, and disposition decisions only remain useful when they can be connected to the correct plant or material. A technically accurate measurement attached to the wrong identity is not reliable traceability.

blocks.alt: Genealogy chain showing source plant, clone tray, transplant batch, flowering room, harvest container, and sample or disposition, with a reminder to preserve source and new identity, location, time, quantity where relevant, responsible record, and the relationship between identifiers at each transition.
blocks.caption: A new identifier should extend the genealogy. It should not erase the relationship to the source material.

items.title: Verify the source
items.body: Match the physical identifier to the controlled work order or record before movement, transformation, sampling, or container change.

items.title: Verify the destination or new container
items.body: Confirm the intended room, location, container, batch, lot, or other destination identity before the transition occurs.

items.title: Preserve the relationship
items.body: When a new identifier is created, link it to the source identity through the facility's controlled record rather than discarding the earlier history.

items.title: Record the event
items.body: Capture the required movement or transformation event, time, location, quantity or count where applicable, and responsible person/system.

items.title: Reconcile after the transition
items.body: Check that the physical state and controlled record now describe the same material and location.

left.label: Traceable transition
left.body: A harvest container receives a new identifier that is recorded as derived from the source plants or batch, preserving the relationship through the harvest event.

right.label: Broken genealogy
right.body: The old identifier is removed, a new label is applied, and no controlled record links the new container to the source material.

blocks.title: The tag and room-move order disagree
blocks.setting: A plant group is ready to move, but the physical tag does not match the batch identifier on the work order. The destination room has space and the schedule is already behind.
blocks.prompt: What is the correct first action?
options: Move the plants and correct the record later
Use cultivar appearance to decide which identity is probably correct
Pause the affected movement and resolve the identity mismatch through the controlled process before genealogy is lost
Remove both identifiers and issue a new one
blocks.answer: Pause the affected movement and resolve the identity mismatch through the controlled process before genealogy is lost.
blocks.feedback: Once an identity transition occurs, reconstructing the correct source can become harder or impossible. The mismatch should be resolved before movement.

blocks.title: Build a propagation-to-harvest genealogy
blocks.instructions: Use a mock set of source-plant, clone-tray, transplant-batch, room-movement, harvest-container, and sample records to reconstruct one complete material lineage.
prompts: Identify each controlled identity in sequence.
Mark every point where a new identifier was created.
Show the record that links each new identifier to the prior identity.
Find one planted break or ambiguous transition.
State what should have been verified before the affected transition occurred.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: Traceability is not a label collection. It is a reconstructable chain of identity and events. Verify before transitions and preserve the relationship between old and new identifiers.
